input: words is an Array of at most 10000 lowercase ASCII strings, each length in [0,1000]. Duplicate words and differing lengths are accepted. Integer inputs, when present, are primitive safe-integer Numbers excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, proxies, subclasses or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The integer number of equivalence groups under arbitrary swaps between positions of the SAME index parity within a word. Even-position and odd-position letter multisets must separately match. Word order is irrelevant, duplicate equivalent words count once, and empty input returns 0.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, caller containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state and separate calls share no mutable result state. Each word gets a fresh 52-entry frequency Array. The group set stores an immutable tuple signature in Python and a comma-delimited numeric signature string in JavaScript; neither exposes mutable frequency state.
numeric: The slot is26*(index mod 2)+(character code-97), always in [0,51]. Counts are at most 1000. The 52 comma-delimited integers form an injective signature with at most 259 characters, including separators; no ambiguous raw concatenation or arithmetic hash is used.
complexity: O(total input characters+52*word count+1) expected time including signature construction/hashing. Retained signatures use O(52*group count+1) bounded-size storage, with one O(52) scratch array live at a time. Total scratch allocations across words are charged. Map/set operation costs assume ordinary average O(1) lookup; target-runtime behavior must be qualified, and universal ECMAScript constant-time guarantees or adversarial collision resistance are not claimed.
